children: The rupiah's depreciation was in line with other regional currencies, a Bank Indonesia official said on Thursday after it fell more than 0.5% against the US dollar, adding that the central bank remained consistent in its market intervention measures to support the currency.
Erwin Gunawan Hutapea, BI's head of monetary management, blamed the rupiah's
depreciation on capital outflows caused by rising US yields, worries about the Middle East conflict and domestic US dollar purchases by importers.
